title: Power Platform: secure Dataverse records with column-based filtering
summary: The roadmap facts and documented preview controls are supported, including additive access on existing ownership models and the System Administrator requirement. The solution-deployment explanation needs an additional Microsoft reference, but no blocking factual error was found.

claims.claim: The enhancement secures Dataverse records using column attribute values rather than traditional ownership.
claims.quote: This enhancement introduces column-based security filtering, enabling records to be secured using attribute values rather than traditional ownership.

claims.claim: Security administrators can define access using business dimensions such as region or department.
claims.quote: This allows security admins to define access based on business dimensions such as region or department

claims.claim: Reporting and aggregated datasets without natural record ownership are intended use cases.
claims.quote: making it ideal for scenarios where record ownership does not exist—such as reporting and aggregated datasets.

claims.claim: The planned approach removes artificial ownership or complex sharing models and simplifies security administration at scale.
claims.quote: By eliminating the need for artificial ownership or complex sharing models, this approach simplifies security administration, improves scalability

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027, not a committed availability date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and does not specify sovereign-cloud availability.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents filter-based security as a preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: Record Filters use FetchXML to identify qualifying records.
claims.quote: Record Filter: Uses FetchXML to identify records that qualify for access.

claims.claim: Entity Record Filters associate Record Filters with Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: Entity Record Filter: Associates a Record Filter with a Dataverse table.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Filter access is granted through security-role filter privileges rather than by merely creating tables or filter records.
claims.quote: When you associate a filter with a table, Dataverse creates filter privileges. Assign these privileges through security roles.

claims.claim: Filtered record ownership tables have no record owner.
claims.quote: Filtered ownership tables don't use record owners.

claims.claim: Filters can also be applied to user or team and organization record ownership tables.
claims.quote: You can apply filter-based security to user or team, and organization record ownership, and filtered record ownership tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: On user-owned tables filter privileges add access and do not reduce ownership-based access.
claims.quote: They don't replace or reduce access granted through ownership, sharing, or security role privileges.

claims.claim: Filtered ownership table records cannot be shared.
claims.quote: Can't be shared with users or teams.

claims.claim: Filtered ownership table records cannot be assigned.
claims.quote: Can't be assigned to users or teams.

claims.claim: Dataverse grants a system-created All records filter privilege to the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: When you create a filtered record ownership table, Dataverse creates a global All records filter privilege and grants it to the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: The described capability is an access-control model, not an autonomous action mechanism.
claims.quote: When a user accesses data, Dataverse evaluates the filters from the user's security roles and team memberships. A matching filter grants the corresponding data access operation.

claims.claim: The System Administrator security role is required to configure the preview feature and its security roles.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles.

claims.claim: The Power Apps maker path is environment > Solutions > solution > New table > Table (advanced properties) > Record ownership > Filtered (preview).
claims.quote: Select your environment. ... Go to Solutions, open the solution you want or create a new one. ... Select New table ... Table (advanced properties). ... From the Record ownership list, select Filtered (preview).

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters creates a Record Filter with a request body.
claims.quote: Create a recordfilter row. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters creates the association between a filter and a table with a request body.
claims.quote: Create an entity record filter to associate the record filter with the table. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Within a solution the filter creation path is + New > More > Other > Record Filter.
claims.quote: Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select Record Filter.

claims.claim: The corresponding association component is created using + New > More > Other > EntityRecordFilter in the solution.
claims.quote: Return to your Solution. ... Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select EntityRecordFilter.

claims.claim: The security-role path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > role.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... select Environments and then select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Users + permissions and select Security roles. ... Choose the security role you want to edit.

claims.claim: The role-bound AddPrivilegesRole action accepts a Privileges collection of RolePrivilege values at roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole.
claims.quote: Bound actions are invoked by appending the fully qualified action name to the URI representing an entity or collection. ... role | entity ... Privileges | Collection(RolePrivilege)

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterId property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterId | Edm.Guid | The Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterUniqueName property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterUniqueName | Edm.String | The Unique Name for the Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: AddPrivilegesRole adds existing privileges to an existing role.
claims.quote: Adds a set of existing privileges to an existing role.

claims.claim: After opening the role, select the target table and filter privilege, grant it, and assign the role to users or teams.
claims.quote: Open a security role. ... Select the target table. ... Select the filter privilege. ... Grant the privilege to the role. ... Assign the role to users or teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant-wide availability switch for filter-based security as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse filter-based security tenant enable switch PowerShell API pac admin default preview; filtered record ownership Power Platform API PowerShell enable. Read admin/filter-based-security, maker and developer filtered ownership guides; pac admin search excerpts. No switch documented.

claims.claim: The access control requires administrator configuration of filters and security-role privileges, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles. ... After creating the record filter and entity record filter, grant the filter ... in a security role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate feature-specific licence or licence change has not been published, so the feature-specific licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: filtered record ownership licensing pricing general availability. Read filter-based-security, maker/developer filtered ownership, data-platform-entity-licenses, and pricing-billing-skus. These give baseline table licensing but no separate feature licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Baseline Dataverse table licensing continues to apply.
claims.quote: App makers can use most of the tables available within Microsoft Dataverse (including custom tables and tables that are part of the Common Data Model) to create apps and flows for users who have a Power Apps or Power Automate license.

claims.claim: Dataverse storage capacity accounting applies to the tables.
claims.quote: All Dataverse tables, including system tables, are included in the storage capacity reports.

claims.claim: Feature-specific general availability pricing is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: filtered record ownership licensing pricing general availability. Opened the feature's admin, maker and developer guides, License requirements for tables and Licensing overview for Microsoft Power Platform; none states feature-specific GA pricing.

claims.claim: Record Filters and Entity Record Filters are solution components.
claims.quote: An unmanaged solution and its unique name. All solution components created by the examples are associated with this solution.

claims.claim: These solution components can travel with solutions through application lifecycle management deployments.
claims.quote: Solutions are the mechanism for implementing application lifecycle management (ALM) in Power Apps and Power Automate. ... The purpose of having components is ... so that it can be exported, imported
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm to sources for the statement that solution components can be exported, imported and deployed through ALM.

claims.claim: Separate preview enablement and rollout mechanics are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: filtered record ownership rollout default; filter-based security enable. Read the admin filter-based-security and maker/developer filtered ownership guides. They describe configuration but give no separate preview enablement setting or rollout mechanics.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that roadmap item 577860 is identical to the documented preview.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "577860" Dataverse. Read the supplied roadmap record and admin, maker and developer preview guides; none explicitly cross-identifies the preview with the roadmap item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Effective filter access combines privileges from users' assigned security roles and team memberships.
claims.quote: Dataverse combines all authorized filters from the user's security roles and team memberships. A record that matches any authorized filter receives the corresponding access.

claims.claim: For filtered ownership tables, filter privileges are the exclusive basis of record access rather than ownership-based access.
claims.quote: Only filtered record ownership tables rely exclusively on filter privileges for record access.

controlChecks.governs: Tables with filtered record ownership and their record filters
